city.name: Lisbon
city.tagline: Seven hills, tiled façades and Atlantic light at the mouth of the Tagus.

dayPass.label: Carris/Metro 24-hour Pass
dayPass.detail: Unlimited metro, bus, tram and funicular for 24 hours.

passes.label: Lisboa Card (24h)
passes.detail: Free entry to Jerónimos, Belém Tower, the Tile Museum, Santa Justa Lift and the Pantheon, plus unlimited metro, bus and tram.

passes.label: Lisboa Card (48h)
passes.detail: As the 24h card, valid for 48 hours.

passes.label: Lisboa Card (72h)
passes.detail: As the 24h card, valid for 72 hours.

hotels.name: Lost Inn Lisbon Hostel
hotels.summary: Hostel in a Chiado townhouse with a river-view terrace.

hotels.name: Home Lisbon Hostel
hotels.summary: Family-run hostel with a home-cooked 'Mamma's dinner', steps from Baixa-Chiado metro.

hotels.name: ibis Lisboa Liberdade
hotels.summary: Plain, reliable rooms just off Avenida da Liberdade.

hotels.name: Hotel Lisboa Tejo
hotels.summary: Azulejo-trimmed hotel a block from Rossio, with an 18th-century well in the lobby.

hotels.name: My Story Hotel Rossio
hotels.summary: Bright rooms right on Rossio square, above two metro lines.

hotels.name: Memmo Alfama
hotels.summary: Whitewashed boutique hotel with a terrace pool over Alfama's rooftops.

hotels.name: Bairro Alto Hotel
hotels.summary: An 18th-century palace on Praça Luís de Camões with a sunset rooftop bar.

attractions.name: Jerónimos Monastery
attractions.summary: A Manueline masterpiece of rope-carved limestone cloisters, paid for with spice-route pepper.
attractions.tip: The church is free; the cloister is the ticketed part — and the reason to come.

attractions.name: Belém Tower
attractions.summary: Fortified 1519 watchtower in the Tagus, where caravels once set out.
attractions.tip: Capacity is capped; arrive at opening or settle for the outside.

attractions.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
attractions.summary: A 52-metre stone prow of navigators, with a compass-rose map set into the plaza.

attractions.name: São Jorge Castle
attractions.summary: Moorish hilltop citadel of peacocks and ramparts with the widest view over the Baixa.
attractions.tip: Ride tram 12 or the free Baixa elevators up; walk down through Alfama.

attractions.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
attractions.summary: Bougainvillea-draped terrace and azulejo panels over Alfama's terracotta roofs.

attractions.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
attractions.summary: The highest viewpoint in the city — castle, river and bridge in one frame at sunset.

attractions.name: National Tile Museum
attractions.summary: Five centuries of azulejos in a convent with a gilded baroque chapel.
attractions.tip: Don't miss the 23-metre panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon upstairs.

attractions.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
attractions.summary: An oil magnate's collection, from Egyptian antiquities to Lalique jewels, in a modernist garden.

attractions.name: MAAT
attractions.wiki: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
attractions.summary: Wave-roofed riverside museum whose rooftop doubles as a walkable viewing deck.

attractions.name: LX Factory
attractions.summary: Converted textile works of bookshops, studios and cafés under the 25 de Abril bridge.

attractions.name: Praça do Comércio
attractions.summary: Vast riverfront square entered through the triumphal Rua Augusta Arch.

attractions.name: Santa Justa Lift
attractions.summary: Neo-Gothic iron elevator linking the Baixa to the Carmo ruins.

attractions.name: Carmo Convent Ruins
attractions.summary: A roofless Gothic nave left open to the sky since the 1755 earthquake.

attractions.name: Lisbon Cathedral (Sé)
attractions.summary: Fortress-like Romanesque cathedral, with Roman and Moorish layers excavated in the cloister.

attractions.name: National Pantheon
attractions.summary: A baroque dome with a terrace view over the Tagus — and the tomb of Amália Rodrigues.

attractions.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
attractions.summary: A vast central tank of sharks, rays and sunfish ringed by four ocean habitats.

eateries.name: Manteigaria
eateries.dish: Pastel de nata, warm from the oven
eateries.summary: A bell rings each time a fresh tray of natas comes out.

eateries.name: Café A Brasileira
eateries.summary: Art-nouveau café of 1905; Fernando Pessoa's bronze still has a seat outside.

eateries.name: Pastéis de Belém
eateries.summary: The recipe is still a secret kept by three bakers. Sit inside — the queue is for takeaway.

eateries.name: O Trevo
eateries.summary: Stand-up counter where Lisbon eats its bifana with a cold imperial.

eateries.name: Time Out Market
eateries.summary: The Ribeira market hall, given over to the city's best-known chefs.

eateries.name: Zé da Mouraria
eateries.dish: Bacalhau with chickpeas — portions for two
eateries.summary: Lunch-only tasca with shared tables and enormous platters.

eateries.name: Páteo 13
eateries.summary: A courtyard grill in Alfama's lanes, smoke drifting over plastic chairs.

eateries.name: Taberna da Rua das Flores
eateries.summary: Tiny, no-reservations tavern reinventing Lisbon small plates.

eateries.name: Ao 26 – Vegan Food Project
eateries.summary: Vegan cooking with Portuguese roots, on a quiet Chiado street.

eateries.name: Enoteca de Belém
eateries.dish: Octopus with sweet potato & Alentejo wines
eateries.summary: Wine bar a lane back from the monastery, with a long Portuguese list.

eateries.name: Tasca do Chico
eateries.summary: Cramped, smoky tasca where amateurs stand up to sing fado.

eateries.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
eateries.dish: Garlic prawns, crab & a prego to finish
eateries.summary: Lisbon's seafood institution — take a number and wait.

eateries.name: Belcanto
eateries.summary: Two Michelin stars, a few doors from the opera house.

markets.name: Feira da Ladra
markets.crafts: Azulejos, vinyl, military surplus and curios — Tuesdays & Saturdays
markets.summary: The 'thieves' market', spread over the square behind the Pantheon.

markets.name: A Vida Portuguesa
markets.crafts: Claus Porto soap, sardine tins, Bordallo ceramics
markets.summary: Heritage Portuguese brands in a former perfume warehouse.

markets.name: Embaixada
markets.crafts: Portuguese designers in a neo-Moorish palace
markets.summary: Concept store gallery around a palace courtyard.

markets.name: Conserveira de Lisboa
markets.summary: Paper-wrapped tins tied with string, sold over a 1930s counter.

markets.name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
markets.crafts: Neighbourhood food market with petisco counters
markets.summary: A locals' market hall that turns into a wine bar after dark.

activities.name: Fado Dinner at Clube de Fado
activities.pitch: a fado dinner in an Alfama cellar
activities.summary: Candlelit dinner and sets from Lisbon's finest fadistas in a vaulted cellar.

activities.name: Azulejo Painting Workshop
activities.summary: Paint and glaze your own tile with a ceramicist; it's fired and ready next day.

activities.name: Private Tascas & Petiscos Food Walk
activities.summary: Seven stops through Mouraria and Alfama with a local food writer.

activities.name: Sunset Sailing on the Tagus
activities.pitch: a sunset sail on the Tagus
activities.summary: Two hours under sail past Belém and beneath the 25 de Abril bridge.

activities.name: Tuk-tuk Tour of the Seven Hills
activities.pitch: a tuk-tuk tour of the seven hills
activities.summary: Electric tuk-tuk loop of miradouros your legs would rather skip.
